deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page carries out Gauss's plane-coordinate computation of a triangulation chain north of Hamburg: Hamburg – Lübeck – Segeberg – Bungsberg – Hohenhorst – Sprenge – Fackebierg – Lysabbel. These are stations of Schumacher's Holstein/Danish chain. The coordinates are those of Gauss's Hannover system, in metres, with origin at Göttingen; x is negative to the north and y is the transverse coordinate. Hamburg = (−224710.000, −1841.000).

The scale side Hamburg–Segeberg is log s = 4.6858114. This is 4.6859017 − 0.0000903, the 'neuere Angabe' noted on p.37 ('um 903 Einheiten kleiner'). The next page (p.39) repeats the work on a revised basis (Hoisbüttel/Eichede, Braak base).

A. STATION LISTS (left column).
- For each station Gauss lists the adjusted spherical direction t (azimuth) to each neighbour.
- He then lists the correction δ, the plane (projected) azimuth T = t + δ, and log10 of the side.
- Check: reciprocal plane azimuths differ by exactly 180°, e.g. Bungsberg→Fackebierg 177°52'19.744 and Fackebierg→Bungsberg 357°52'19.744.
- The correction (my notation, verified on every line) is
  δ(1→2) = −(ρ/(2R²))·(x2−x1)·(2y1+y2)/3,
  where log(ρ/2R²) = 1.40334−10 near Hamburg, decreasing to 1.40326 at Fackebierg (latitude-dependent radius R).
- Example, H→S: log|Δx| = 4.63482, +1.40334 = 6.03816. Then log|(2yH+yS)/3| = log 9238.0 = 3.96558. The sum 0.00374 gives 1.0086'', entered as −1.008.
- S→H: log|(yH+2yS)/3| = log 16635 = 4.22102, giving +1.816.
- This is the arc-to-chord ('t−T') reduction of the conformal (Gauss–Krüger type) projection, to the R⁻² term. It is the same expression as on p.37 ('−(x'−x)η …').

B. EACH TRIANGLE ('Dreieck 1–5'). Each block contains the following steps.
1. Plane angles are taken as differences of plane azimuths. They sum to exactly 180°0'0''.000.
   (i) H 25°7'18.408, L 54°29'4.113, S 100°23'37.479.
   (ii) L 76°24'35.153, S 66°18'32.529, B 37°16'52.318.
   (iii) S 54°45'10.997, B 56°11'35.457, Ho 69°3'13.546.
   (iv) B 26°46'33.409, Ho 109°38'15.675, Sp 43°35'10.916.
   (v) B 54°22'51.641, Sp 73°27'40.780, F 52°9'27.579.
2. Sine rule in logarithms from the known side:
   - Dreieck 1: log c − log sin L = 4.7752093; adding log sin S gives HL = 4.7680239; adding log sin H gives LS = 4.4031316.
   - The other triangles are analogous: LB 4.5826199, SB 4.6085212; SHo 4.5577716, BHo 4.5502611; BSp 4.6857357, HoSp 4.3654576; BF 4.7699225, SpF 4.6983138.
3. Coordinate differences: Δx = s·cos T, Δy = s·sin T, from log s + log cos T and log s + log sin T, with 'n' marking negative values.
   - Dreieck 1 gives H→L (−35808.191, −46408.309), L→S (−7325.814, +24216.849), H→S (−43134.020, −22191.472).
4. The new point is computed from both known vertices. The two results (differing by ≤0.015 m) are meaned to give the coordinate table:
   - Lübeck (−260518.197, −48249.315)
   - Segeberg (−267844.013, −24032.469)
   - Bungsberg (−298706.017, −50411.630)
   - Hohenhorst (−302857.493, −15152.508)
   - Sprenge (−325468.331, −9964.587)
   - Fackebierg (−357539.288, −48225.676)
5. Spherical excess: ε = (ρ/2R²)·a·b·sin C, in logs.
   - Dreieck 1: log(HL·sin L) = 4.67863, + log LS 4.40313, + const 1.40333 gives 0.48509, i.e. ε = 3''.056.
   - Likewise ε2 = 2''.381 (LB sin B · SB), ε3 = 3''.031 (SB sin B · BHo), ε4 = 1''.963 (BSp sin Sp · HoSp), ε5 = 5''.875 (BF sin F · SpF).
6. The same columns hold, for each side, log|Δx|+const and log|(2y1+y2)/3|, log|(y1+2y2)/3|. These produce all the δ's in the station lists.

C. CONSISTENCY (my verification). The spherical angles from the uncorrected directions sum to 180° + ε exactly:
- (i) 25°7'18.969 + 54°29'7.829 + 100°23'36.258 = 180°0'3.056
- (ii) 180°0'2.381
- (iii) 180°0'3.032
- (iv) 180°0'1.963
- (v) 180°0'5.875
So the direction reductions and the excess computation agree to the last digit.

D. LYSABBEL (only provisional, directions to 0.1''). Angles from the plane azimuths are Sp 57°27'37'', F 61°49'58'', giving Ly ≈ 60°42'25''. This matches 352°34' − 291°51' = 60°43'. Approximate coordinates (−375509, −3438.2).
errors: Lysabbel side logarithms are interchanged in the station lists. By the sine rule, Sprenge–Lysabbel (opposite the 61°50' angle at Fackebierg) must be the longer side, 4.70299; Fackebierg–Lysabbel must be 4.68357. The page lists Sprenge–Lysabbel 4.6835717 and Fackebierg–Lysabbel 4.7029945, and the Lysabbel list repeats the swap. Page 39 has them correctly (4.7031640, 4.6837476). The provisional Lysabbel coordinates (≈ −375509, −3439) agree with the correct assignment, so the slip is in the labels only.

Dreieck 3: log sin of the azimuth S→Ho (165°46') is positive, yet it appears marked 'n' (9.3906395n). The coordinate difference actually used, +8879.961, has the correct sign, so this is a notation slip or misreading only.
Dreieck 4: Δy for Bungsberg→Sprenge appears written as −40447.047 but must be +40447.047 (sin 123°29' > 0). The coordinate Sprenge y = −9964.587 was computed with the + sign.
Lysabbel x is written without its minus sign (375509 for −375509).
Closure differences between the two determinations of each point are ≤0.015 m and are meaned. These are not errors.
Excess constant 1.40331–1.40334 is used inconsistently by ±1–2 units in the 5th decimal. This is negligible (<0.001'').

results.what: Reduction of observed (spheroidal) directions to the plane of the projection: δ = −(ρ/2R²)(x2−x1)(2y1+y2)/3, applied at both ends of each side
results.modern_name: arc-to-chord (t−T) correction of the Gauss conformal / Gauss–Krüger projection (first-order term)
results.usually_credited_to: C.F. Gauss (Hannover survey, 1820s); published form by Schreiber (1866) and Krüger (1912)

results.what: Spherical excess ε = ρ·ab·sinC/(2R²) with latitude-dependent R

results.modern_name: network junction of the Hannover and Danish surveys

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine computing page of Gauss's Hannover triangulation, linking to Schumacher's Danish chain. The direction-reduction formula of his conformal projection and the spherical excess are well known to be Gauss's. The only interest is the clean internal consistency and the documentation of the reduction scheme in use.
